verses.1: But the Lord, answering Job out of the whirlwind, said:
verses.2: Gird your waist like a man. I will question you, and you must answer me.
verses.3: Will you make my judgment null and void; and will you condemn me so that you may be justified?
verses.4: And do you have an arm like God, or a voice like thunder?
verses.5: Envelop yourself with splendor, and raise yourself up on high, and be glorious, and put on splendid garments.
verses.6: Scatter the arrogant with your wrath, and, when you see all the arrogant, humble them.
verses.7: Look down upon each of the arrogant and confound them, and crush the impious in their place.
verses.8: Hide them in the dust together and plunge their faces into the pit.
verses.9: Then I will confess that your right hand is able to save you.
verses.10: Behold, the behemoth, whom I created along with you, eats hay like an ox.
verses.11: His strength is in his lower back, and his power is in the center of his abdomen.
verses.12: He draws up his tail like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs have been drawn together.
verses.13: His bones are like pipes of brass; his cartilage is like plates of iron.
verses.14: He is the beginning of the ways of God, who made him; he will use him as his sword.
verses.15: The mountains bring forth grass for him; all the beasts of the field will play there.
verses.16: He sleeps in the shadows, under the cover of branches, and in moist places.
verses.17: The shadows cover his shadow; the willows of the brook will encircle him.
verses.18: Behold, he will drink a river and not be amazed, and he has confidence that the Jordan could flow into his mouth.
verses.19: He will seize him through his eyes, as if with a hook, and he will bore through his nostrils, as if with stakes.
verses.20: Can you draw out the leviathan with a hook, and can you bind his tongue with a cord?
verses.21: Can you place a ring in his nose, or bore through his jaw with an arm band?
verses.22: Will he offer many prayers to you, or speak to you quietly?
verses.23: Will he form a covenant with you, and will you accept him as a servant forever?
verses.24: Will you play with him as with a bird, or tether him for your handmaids?
verses.25: Will your friends cut him into pieces, will dealers distribute him?
verses.26: Will you fill up bags with his hide, and let his head be used as a home for fishes?
verses.27: Place your hand upon him; remember the battle and speak no more.
verses.28: Behold, his hope will fail him, and in the sight of all, he will be thrown down. [ Job 41 ]
